title: Fibonacci EA v5.0 Hard Stop Loss Reduction Test (15.0 -> 12.0 pips)
research_question: Does reducing InpMaxSLPips from 15.0 to 12.0 pips reduce average loss severity without significantly degrading the ~79% win rate, lowering max equity drawdown below 7.35% and improving overall profit factor on GBPUSD M15?
hypothesis: Decreasing InpMaxSLPips from 15.0 to 12.0 pips will cut the average loss size from ~$73.50 down to ~$55.00, reducing the required mathematical breakeven win rate to ~71% and decreasing max equity drawdown while maintaining net profit above baseline $577.65.

facts: EXP-0008 demonstrated a 1:2.76 loss-to-win asymmetry (avg win $26.59 vs avg loss -$73.50) with InpMaxSLPips=15.0.
EXP-0012 and EXP-0015 proved that despite maintaining a 76-80% win rate out-of-sample, the rigid -$70.50 loss per trade pushed the mathematical breakeven requirement above 78%.
The Fibonacci entry zones (38.2%, 50.0%, 61.8%) have an InpFibBuffer of 5.0 pips, so a 12.0 pip stop still provides 7 pips of breathing room beyond the buffer zone.
inferences: If a pullback trade penetrates more than 12 pips against the Fibonacci level on M15 GBPUSD, the reversal premise is already invalidated.
Cutting the stop loss to 12.0 pips will cut loss severity by 20% without materially increasing the rate of stop-outs.
evidence: EXP-0008 total_trades=272, profit_factor=1.39, average_loss_trade=-73.50, total_net_profit=577.65, equity_drawdown_maximal_percent=7.35

independent_variables.name: InpMaxSLPips
independent_variables.rationale: Tighten hard stop loss from 15.0 to 12.0 pips to reduce loss severity per losing trade from -$73.50 to ~$55.00.

assumptions: Broker stop level allows 12-pip stops during normal London/NY spread conditions.
expected_observations: Average loss size will decrease from -$73.50 to less than -$60.00.
Total net profit will remain above or near baseline $577.65.
falsification_conditions: Win rate collapses below 70.0% due to premature stop-outs by market noise.
Maximum equity drawdown exceeds 8.0%, breaching the prop firm guard threshold.
